prompts.body: Under 30 | Under £5 Greek Doner Kebab – Inspired by @mezemike Serves 4 | Ready in under 30 minutes The recipe comes well under £5 after only using 1/4 cucumber & onions but pricing is easier and more transparent this way, if you can grab a fresh lemon for around 30p extra, if takes it to a whole new level. Ingredients – Greek Spiced Doner Meat: 500 g pork mince – £2.25 1 onion – blended finely (95p for 3) 1 tbsp olive oil ½ tbsp garlic granules ½ tsp salt ½ tsp black pepper ½ tbsp paprika ½ tbsp dried oregano ½ tsp cinnamon 2 tbsp Greek or natural yoghurt 2 tbsp tomato purée Flatbreads: 120 g plain flour (1 cup) 2 tbsp olive oil 1 tsp flaky salt 120g natural yoghurt (1/2 cup) Roasted Veg: 1 red pepper – £0.67 1 onion – cut into wedges Oil, pinch salt and pepper Tzatziki: 200 ml natural yoghurt – £0.55 Juice of ½ lemon (or a tsp cider vinegar) 1 tbsp olive oil ¼ cucumber – seeds removed & finely diced – £0.89 15–20 fresh mint leaves OR 1 tsp dried mint Salt to taste Total shop: £5.31 Method – 1️⃣ Prep the Doner Meat: Add the pork mince to a bowl. Blend the onion until very finely chopped or pulped. Add to the mince along with all remaining doner ingredients. Mix really well until smooth and well combined. 2️⃣ Shape & Bake: Lay out two sheets of baking paper. Spread the meat very thinly into a rectangle. Roll up tightly like a sausage using the paper. Bake at 180°C (fan) for 30 minutes. 3️⃣ Roast the Veg: Cut the red pepper into sixths. Cut the onion into 6 wedges. Add to a tray, drizzle with oil, season. Roast alongside the doner for 25–30 minutes. 4️⃣ Flatbreads: Mix flour, yoghurt, olive oil, and salt into a dough. Knead briefly until smooth. Divide into 4 balls. Roll out thin and dry-fry in a hot pan 1–2 mins per side until cooked. 5️⃣ Finish the Doner: Unwrap the doner from baking paper. Place back on the tray, unrolled. Return to the oven to keep warm — edges will crisp slightly (delicious). 6️⃣ Tzatziki: Mix yoghurt, lemon juice, olive oil, cucumber, mint, and salt. Chill if time allows. 7️⃣ Serve: Fill warm flatbreads with crispy doner meat. Add roasted peppers & onions. Drizzle generously with tzatziki. Much Love, Jade x

people.line: I’m the founder and CEO of Thrive Global, a behavior change technology company with the mission of improving health and helping us move from merely surviving to thriving. I also founded The Huffington Post and have written 15 books, including Thrive and The Sleep Revolution. I’m originally from Greece (and still have the accent to prove it!). When I was 17, I moved to England and studied economics at Cambridge University, where I frankly spent most of my time debating at the Cambridge Union. I live in New York but also spend time in Los Angeles, and love being a Yiayia (Greek for grandmother) to my almost three-year-old grandson Alexander and his newborn sister Annabel. My journey to focusing on health began with a fall. In April 2007, I collapsed from exhaustion and burnout and hit my head on my desk on the way down, breaking my cheekbone. In the wake of my fall, I found myself going from doctor to doctor to find out what was wrong. Doctors’ waiting rooms were good places for me to ask myself a lot of questions about the kind of life I was living. After all the tests, it turned out nothing was wrong. Except for the fact that everything was wrong. I was suffering from an acute case of burnout. I had bought into the myth that burnout was the price I had to pay for success. I became more and more passionate about the five daily habits that drive so much of our health: nutrition, exercise, sleep, stress management and connection. That led me to write Thrive and The Sleep Revolution. The books struck a chord, but I wanted to go beyond speaking and writing to helping people move from awareness to action. So in 2016 I founded Thrive Global, which helps people transform their health by combining Microsteps — small, science-backed daily steps — with technology, storytelling and community. And last year, with the OpenAI Startup Fund, we launched Thrive AI Health to build an AI health coach to democratize access to health coaching.

prompts.body: If you're building something new right now, I'd bet your week looks a lot like this. You get home from the job that pays the bills, open the laptop, and do the same thing you did last night, answering the same customer question, fixing the same page, sending the same follow-up to someone who probably won't reply, while everyone online seems to be announcing their big launch. It feels like nothing is happening. I know that feeling. We started Quest making protein bars by hand in a small kitchen. We had no idea if anyone would care. Nobody was clapping. There was no launch moment. There was just the next batch. I wish someone had told me back then that boredom is what progress feels like from the inside. Answer that customer’s question one more time and you learn a little more about what's really bugging people. Fix the landing page again and it gets a little easier to buy from you. If you keep going, one of those reps turns into the thing people pay for. If you stop, you never find out which one it was. It might never get exciting. You just get better at the boring thing, and one day the boring thing starts paying you back. If you want help carrying some of that load, that's what my free masterclass is for.
